input.question: Why is this year's flu vaccine so bad?
input.ground_truth: The flu vaccine is ordered based on the strains of flu circulating in the world approximately 6 months in advance of the US flu season to allow time to make the vaccine, distribute it, and administer it. In the time between the moment that the target flu strains were selected for inclusion into the vaccine and now the virus strains mutated and are now different from what is in the vaccine. This is not the first time it has happened and so long as the production cycle is 4-6 months it will continue to happen.

Okay! Imagine you and your friends want to play a game outside, but this year, some of the balls you use to play are old and don’t work as well as new ones. The flu vaccine is like a special shield to help your body fight the flu (a sickness that makes you feel really bad). 

This year, the scientists who make the flu vaccine guessed what the flu would look like, but the flu changed a little bit after they made the shield. So, the shield doesn’t fit the flu as well as it should. That’s why some people say this year’s flu vaccine isn’t working as well as it usually does. 

But don’t worry! The vaccine still helps some people, and it helps scientists learn how to make even better shields next year.
